newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares take a beating, as govt dashes hopes.
newsitem.headline: India shares take a beating, as govt dashes hopes.

text.p: ** (1300 GMT) - Major Indian bourses react sharply as
govt fails to deliver much-publicised market "package"
** Bombay share index ends 3.63 pct down at 3,382.47
** Belied hopes of market policy incentives triggers nervous
sell-off in index stocks by speculators
** Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda goes to Davos for World
Economic Forum leaving stunned traders in his wake
** National bourse's 50-stock index falls 27.35 points, or
2.73 pct, to 972.65 in volumes of 17.10 billion rupees
** Delhi index loses 2.65 pct to 731.65, Madras index 2.07
pct to 3,298.07 and Calcuta index 2.68 pct to 440.66
Indian shares tumbled on Friday in nervous selling as traders offloaded blue chips after eagerly awaited market policy initiatives failed to come through.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top 30-share index ended 3.63 pct lower at 3,382.47 after plunging 148.80 points, or 4.24 percent, in a session traders described as "nerve-wracking".

Traders' hopes for a new policy package that would boost the capital markets collapsed after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said late on Thursday that it was actually made up of a series of measures announced in January.

"We have seen the initial break down. Everyone seems to be waiting for the others to react. There's more confusion than anything else," said chief dealer Sanjeev Sanghvi at foreign brokerage James Capel B&K.

Last Monday, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said the government would announce new economic measures before he departed with Chidambaram for the World Economic Forum summit at Davos in Switzerland on Friday.
But traders were disappointed by the actual announcement.
"It's very irresponsible on the part of the prime minister," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at brokers Pashupati Advani.
